title: Associated primes of a Cohen–Macaulay local ring are minimal primes
statement: Let $(T,\mathfrak n)$ be a Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] (a Noetherian commutative ring with exactly one maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$) of Krull dimension $e=\dim T$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] (finite, as $T$ is Noetherian local), and assume that $T$ is Cohen–Macaulay in the sense that $\operatorname{depth}(T)\ge e$ [def-weil-pbc-depth], that is, $\mathfrak n$ contains a $T$-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] of length $e$. Let $\mathfrak p\subset T$ be a prime ideal for which there is $z\in T$ with $\operatorname{Ann}_T(z)=\{a\in T: az=0\}=\mathfrak p$ (an associated prime of $T$). Then $\mathfrak p$ is a minimal prime ideal of $T$ (no prime ideal of $T$ is strictly contained in $\mathfrak p$).

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0BUS (lemma-CM-ass-minimal-support, line 25108), the assertion that p is minimal in Supp(M), for M = T (Supp(T) = Spec T, dim Supp(T) = dim T; T is a Cohen-Macaulay module over itself since depth(T) <= dim T, Tag 00LK); Cohen-Macaulay local ring as in Definition Tag 00N8 (definition-local-ring-CM, line 25308)

proof.text: ($\dim(T/\mathfrak p)\ge e$.) $T$ is a finite $T$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], generated by $1$, and $\mathfrak p=\operatorname{Ann}_T(z)$ with $z\in T$ is an associated prime of the $T$-module $T$. By [lem-weil-pbc-depth-le-dim-associated-prime], applied to the Noetherian local ring $T$, the finite module $M=T$ and $\mathfrak p$, we get $\dim(T/\mathfrak p)\ge\operatorname{depth}(T)$, where $\operatorname{depth}(T)$ is the depth of $T$ as a module over itself [def-weil-pbc-depth]. By hypothesis $\operatorname{depth}(T)\ge e$, so $\dim(T/\mathfrak p)\ge e$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0BUS (lemma-CM-ass-minimal-support, line 25108), proof lines 25119-25132, for M = T, first sentence (Lemma lemma-depth-dim-associated-primes, Tag 0BK4)

proof.text: ($\mathfrak p$ is minimal.) Suppose a prime ideal $\mathfrak q$ of $T$ satisfies $\mathfrak q\subsetneq\mathfrak p$. Since $\dim(T/\mathfrak p)\ge e$ and $e$ is an integer $\ge0$, by the definition of the Krull dimension as a supremum [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] the ring $T/\mathfrak p$ has a chain of prime ideals of length $n\ge e$, and keeping its first $e+1$ members one of length exactly $e$. The prime ideals of $T/\mathfrak p$ are the $\mathfrak P/\mathfrak p$ with $\mathfrak P$ a prime of $T$ containing $\mathfrak p$, with inclusions preserved and reflected, so this chain is $\mathfrak P_0/\mathfrak p\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak P_e/\mathfrak p$ with primes $\mathfrak p\subseteq\mathfrak P_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak P_e$ of $T$. Then $\mathfrak q\subsetneq\mathfrak p\subseteq\mathfrak P_0$ gives the chain $\mathfrak q\subsetneq\mathfrak P_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak P_e$ of prime ideals of $T$ of length $e+1$, so $\dim T\ge e+1>e=\dim T$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], a contradiction. Hence no prime ideal of $T$ is strictly contained in $\mathfrak p$: $\mathfrak p$ is a minimal prime of $T$. (This is the source's 'otherwise we would have $\dim(R/\mathfrak p)<\dim(\operatorname{Supp}(M))$' for $M=T$, $\operatorname{Supp}(T)=\operatorname{Spec}T$; the source's bound $\dim(R/\mathfrak p)\le\dim\operatorname{Supp}(M)$ is not needed.)
